rules_applied: JCS sorts object property names by ascending UTF-16 code-unit values, using unsigned numeric comparison independent of locale.
Whitespace is removed; values are otherwise unchanged because all are integers.
JCS recursively sorts every JSON object, including objects nested inside arrays.
Array element order is preserved.
Inside outer, a precedes z by UTF-16 code-unit order.
Inside the first array object, x precedes y; the second object contains only k.
Whitespace is removed; true and null serialize as the literal tokens true and null.
Numbers are serialized according to ECMAScript IEEE-754 double-precision number serialization.
n1: 1e21 is serialized as 1e+21; exponential notation is required at this magnitude and the positive exponent includes +.
n2: 1e-7 remains 1e-7; exponential notation is used for this magnitude.
n3: 0.000001 remains 0.000001; ECMAScript uses decimal notation at exactly this boundary rather than 1e-6.
n4: 100000000000000000000 is the IEEE-754 value 1e20 and serializes as 100000000000000000000 in decimal notation.
n5: -0 serializes as 0; JSON/ECMAScript serialization does not preserve negative zero.
n6: 333333333.33333329 is rounded to the representable IEEE-754 double and serializes as 333333333.3333333.
Whitespace is removed.
JCS sorts raw property names by UTF-16 code units, not locale or Unicode collation.
The resulting order is $ (U+0024), aa (U+0061,U+0061), € (U+20AC), ü (U+00FC).
Thus $ < a < € < ü by the numeric values of their UTF-16 code units.
Non-ASCII characters are emitted as-is; JCS does not apply Unicode normalization.

é (U+00E9) is outside the ASCII control range and is emitted as-is in the JSON text.
The two spaces in s5 are ordinary U+0020 spaces and are emitted unchanged; they are string content, not JSON-token whitespace.

specific_rule_in_doubt: The exact ECMAScript/JCS IEEE-754 shortest-number serialization, especially the boundary behavior for 1e21, 1e-7, exactly 1e-6, and 1e20; these were checked against ECMAScript JSON.stringify behavior, which RFC 8785 normatively relies upon.
